reviews.title: Don’t use this app.
reviews.text:
I used TextFree for several months and paid for a subscription. Recently, my texts started getting restricted when I was communicating with restaurant employees and job applicants. Customer support told me that sending similar messages to multiple people can trigger the security filters, even when the messages are for legitimate business purposes.

This has made the app very inconvenient to use. I’m planning to cancel my subscription and switch to another app. Please keep this in mind if you’re considering TextFree for business communications.

reviews.title: Don’t use it and definitely don’t pay for it
reviews.text: This used to be a good and reliable app, and it’s a shame what it has become. I had my account suddenly banned for accidentally attempting to log into my account with my VPN on, and it only took one time. No warning, no recourse, just a vague error number and no longer able to login until I had to do some searching to find out why. This seems to be happening to many others from the reviews so I’m not alone. Contacts and everything I had for years gone.  The account also seems to just be completely gone now too as I tried waiting it out to see if it would clear and now says the user doesn’t exist. Another (better) app I switched to will just paywall you if the VPN is on and won’t let you use it until you turn it off or pay extra. This is a poor approach to security and bad actors. Please don’t reply to “contact support” that ship has sailed and since it seems my account is now just gone. Maybe instead reevaluate your policies on insta-bans that just drive users away. I’ve moved on and won’t be back to just risk one day my account just being dead again and wondering why.

reviews.title: Would be perfect, except....
reviews.text: I used this app to send a goofy video to my friends from an unknown number. Tested it out by sending to my personal phone number. The service auto-inserts a higher resolution video link and sends an additional text message after the video is sent on the user's behalf. The user should be able to turn this bloatware OFF. First, it interrupts the conversation and kills the vibe. Second, Apple is extremely likely to detect incoming links from unknown numbers as spam. Third, it's tacky to send additional text messages on behalf of the user without their input, and it should be rethought. Fourth, the links reveal what service the user is using to the recipient, which is also tacky. What if I don't want my friends knowing I am using a burner number that's with TextFree? This silly feature turned a fun prank into something not worth doing. Thankfully, I didn't pay for this service. Also, from a business perspective, why spend additional compute resources auto-opting users into a feature that hosts every video they send in the cloud? Your business is paying to host those videos, and I doubt most users want this enabled. A setting to disable this is needed. Oh yeah, one more thing... If this review leads to a product manager adding a toggle that cuts hosting costs and improves the user experience, I’ll accept payment in cash, equity, or one lifetime ad-free burner number. If this feature is added without me being contacted, I will be back....
